newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen mixed to lower in early trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen mixed to lower in early trade.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open mixed to lower with all eyes on the high techs to see whether they can bounce back from a sell-off which undermined the entire market Wednesday.
"The momentum from yesterday carried over into European markets, so I think we will open mixed to lower," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities.
"The key to trading today will be the techs. The market will want to see whether the likes of Intel and Cisco can snap back and show some stability."
Some techs moved higher in after hours trading on Wednesday and overnight in London.

Wachtel said that he did not believe that brokerage stocks would be able to maintain their rally from yesterday, which was sparked by an stock-swap merger announcement by Morgan Stanley Group Inc and Dean Witter Discover. The merger is expected to create a financial powerhouse with a combined market capitalization of $21 billion.
"They had a big pop yesterday, but I doubt they can sustain it today," Wachtel said. "The brokerages will probably come in for some profit-taking."
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average was down 147.54 points, or 0.81 points, 18,034.43.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index was down 10.1 points at 4271.4

Among U.S. shares traded in London, high techs had a small bounce, with Intel Corp up 3/4 at 158. International Business Machines Corp was up 1/2 at 148-1/2 and Microsoft Corp was climbed 3/8 to 98-3/4. Ford Motor Co was down 1/8 at 32-1/4 following a Wall Street Journal report that the company faces $5 million in daily costs from lost production because of a strike at an automotive seat supplier.
The dollar gained strength against the yen in Tokyo. In Europe, it was firm on the yen and off its highs versus the mark.
U.S. Treasuries were thinly mixed, with the long bond unchanged to yield 6.76 percent.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street writes that some of the rumors about mergers among brokerages have been around Wall Street longer than the traders who pass them.
But suddenly yesterday, everyone was taking the chatter a lot more seriously.
In the wake of the news that Morgan Stanley Group Inc and Dean Witter Discover, shares of several Wall Street firms were up sharply as investors concluded that the odds went up for more deals.
